abstract: We present the first reverberation mapping (RM) measurements in the COSMOS field included in the SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project. Using $\sim$6 months of plate-based spectroscopy (from late 2020 to mid-2021) and accompanying ZTF+DECam \emph{gri}-band photometric light curves, we analyze the variability of over 250 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) out to $z \sim 3$. We successfully recover reliable $\lesssim$ 200d time lags for 22 AGNs ($z \lesssim 2.5$) in H$\alpha$, H$\beta$, MgII, or CIV, using a combination of multiple lag detection methods and significance tests. Our measurements are consistent with the radius-luminosity relations from recent large-scale RM programs, providing measured masses of $10^{7-9} M_{\odot}$ for these AGNs. These results and upcoming long-baseline SDSS-V spectroscopy lay the groundwork for large-sample AGN studies in conjunction with other facilities covering the COSMOS field, including the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and Roman Space Telescope.
hook: Black hole masses measured for 22 distant active galaxies in the COSMOS field from light echoes.

readout.label: Active galaxies with reliable time lags

summary: Using about six months of SDSS-V spectra plus ZTF and DECam light curves for over 250 active galactic nuclei, the team recovered reliable time lags for 22. The lags match known radius-luminosity relations and give black hole masses of 10^7 to 10^9 solar masses. The six-month baseline limits detection to short lags and a small fraction of the sample.
title: The SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project: Short Lags in the COSMOS Field
